title: Building a 3D tavern for my RTS from a generated concept image. Process, description + costs included
author: Alarmed_Profit1426
selftext:
This was just a quick experiment to see if I could get a proper interior into the game I am working on without modelling the whole thing by hand. The tavern will act as the hub between campaign story missions. Rough steps that Claude executed end to end:

1. Generated a few tavern concepts with ChatGPT image gen 2.5 until one felt right.
2. Blocked the room out in three.js to match it: walls, floor, beams, fireplace, bar.
3. Made an "empty" version of the concept with all the furniture taken out and projected it onto the room from the camera. Tiling stone and wood textures sit under it so it holds up close, then baked the lighting in.
4. Pulled the objects out of the concept one by one (tables, barrels, shelves, mugs, candles), made a clean 2D image of each and ran them through Meshy to get the 3D models.
5. The people are rigged Meshy models with Mixamo animations, retargeted in Blender.
6. Wrote some basic scripts so patrons wander in off the street and sit down while the barmaid does the rounds.
7. Music from Suno, background chatter and fire from ElevenLabs, plus a few menus.
8. Dropped it into a generated town, so you can walk out the front door and around the streets.

It's still rough in places, but for a test it came out better than I expected. You can walk around it here: [shardsofstone.com/tavern-lab](http://shardsofstone.com/tavern-lab)

Tool & cost breakdown

|What|Usage|Cost|
|:-|:-|:-|
|Meshy|52 objects and 11 people at 30 credits each, plus 11 rigs at 5, about 1,950 credits - some of this is re-used within the game itself anyway.|about $23|
|OpenAI image gen (gpt-image-2.5)|about 70 images: one per object, two room plates, five floor and wall textures, the rug and the street|about $4|
|Suno|12 credits for the music|under $0.10|
|ElevenLabs|two background sound loops|pennies|
|Mixamo|animations|free|
|**Total**||**about $27**|

I spent very little time on this and was surprised by the result when I got back to my laptop.  
  
Happy to go into more detail on any of it.

comments.author: mccoypauley
comments.body:
Incredible seeing this come together.

I'm starting to dig into this myself; I recently used Astra/Sol 6.1 to make a city simulation as a sort of marketing tool for my website's homepage, where it has a minigame. 

For the models of buildings, I had started with some sample models from an open source project, and had Astra (in Ultra mode) alter them/make some new ones. That worked but it was compute-expensive.

What's it like using Meshy? I haven't used it yet, but do you just give it some sample images and it spits out a model that Codex can leverage? You mention animations in Mixamo and the retargeting in Blender. Would I need to study up to understand what "retargeting" means and how to use Blender for the model repairs? (I'm a developer so I could invest time to figure it out, but I just was curious where skilling myself is needed...)

replies.author: Alarmed_Profit1426
replies.body:
Meshy has a UI but I just use get Claude to use it via API, just using image to model. Works well and latest version 7 quality is a huge step up from version 6 (hardly use retries now).

With animating models, meshy can do skeleton rigs and basic animations but they are hit and miss. The latest models can rig and animate pretty much anything with enough iterations. I just asked Opus 5.5 and Sol 6.1 to use blender and visually inspect the models and some keyframes to check it looks correct. There is a blog here that Claude wrote up: https://www.shardsofstone.com/blog/generating-and-rigging-game-ready-3d-units

replies.body: Thanks man for this explainer and the post!
